patch.objective: Recognize depression, hopelessness and ruminative thinking and the risk they carry
secondaryObjectives: Assess suicide risk and build a safety plan in a counseling session

sources.cite: Beck AT, Steer RA, Kovacs M, Garrison B. Hopelessness and eventual suicide: a 10-year prospective study of patients hospitalized with suicidal ideation. Am J Psychiatry 1985;142:559-563: of 207 patients, 14 died by suicide; only the Hopelessness Scale and the BDI pessimism item predicted it, and a hopelessness score of 10 or more identified 91% of them
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the abstract (summarizing fetch). Used only for hopelessness as a risk marker; no scale is given in the case.

sources.cite: Nolen-Hoeksema S, Wisco BE, Lyubomirsky S. Rethinking rumination. Perspect Psychol Sci 2008;3(5):400-424 (doi:10.1111/j.1745-6924.2008.00088.x): rumination predicts the onset of depression and, with negative cognitive styles, its persistence; it impairs problem solving and erodes social support
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the abstract on eScholarship (summarizing fetch).

sources.cite: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JB. The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. J Gen Intern Med 2001;16:606-613: total 0-27; 5, 10, 15 and 20 mark mild, moderate, moderately severe and severe; item 9 (thoughts of being better off dead or of self-harm) counts if present at all
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in an IHS copy of the scoring guide (summarizing fetch with short quotes). A score is a screen, not a diagnosis.

sources.cite: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS), Screen Version: wish to be dead; suicidal thoughts; thoughts with method; intent without plan; intent with plan; suicidal behavior
sources.note: Relayed from the NCMHCE case ncmhce-suicide-safety-plan (re-read 2026-11-11), not re-read here. The questions are paraphrased and asked without asking for details; the screen does not itself set risk levels.

sources.cite: Stanley B, Brown GK. Safety planning intervention: a brief intervention to mitigate suicide risk. Cogn Behav Pract 2012;19:256-264; SPRC summary of the six steps
sources.note: Relayed from the EPPP and NCMHCE sessions (read 2026-11-10), not re-read: warning signs; internal coping; people and places for distraction; people to ask for help; professionals and crisis lines; making the environment safe.

sources.cite: SAMHSA, 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: 'Call or Text 988'
sources.note: Relayed from the NCMHCE case (read 2026-11-11), not re-read.

sources.cite: ACA Code of Ethics (2014): A.1.b (records reflect progress), A.1.c (counseling plans devised jointly and regularly reviewed), A.2.a, A.11.c (termination when the client no longer needs or benefits), B.2.a (serious and foreseeable harm), C.2.g (impairment), E.1.a-b (purpose of assessment; the client's right to know results), H.2.a, H.4.a
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in a state board's copy of the 2014 code (confirmed '© 2014', 'As approved by the ACA Governing Council'; summarizing fetch with short quotes). The current code per counseling.org (read 2026-11-11 for REQ-239), a revision pending.
